notes:
Procurement-heavy, legal + infra involved. Customer is Aurora Payments (enterprise fintech) evaluating Redwood Dedicated with VPC/private control plane. Main ask: formal SLA with uptime target, credit schedule, clearly defined maintenance windows, and tight support response times for P1/P2. Also needs reserved GPU planning for peak payroll cycles (quarterly spikes). Short snippets from calls: "We cannot accept standard 99.9% without commensurate credits"; "must support 95th p99 latency targets for chat under production traffic". SE already ran Dedicated sizing exercise; initial recommendation 12 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs with 2x burst pool. Procurement wants legal language on scheduled maint windows and out-of-band security notifications.

Notes from demo: latency tests hit 95p ~120ms for single-turn chat at 60 concurrent QPS; they require <150ms p95 and <350ms p99 for multi-turn. Throughput target: sustain 200k tokens/minute during payroll batch windows, burst to 500k tokens/min for 30-minute windows. Cost sensitivity moderate; willing to pay for reserved capacity if SLA/credits are acceptable.

Action items: add explicit credit table to SOW, define maintenance windows (monthly 2h off-peak + emergency 48h max notification), formalize response times (P1 1h, P2 4h, P3 24h), provide SOC2 type II and encryption/KMS integration plan.

requirements_summary: Enterprise fintech requiring Dedicated capacity in VPC with strict SLA. Must support real-time chat p95 <150ms, p99 <350ms under production concurrency, throughput 200k tokens/min sustained with 500k tokens/min burst. Reserved GPU plan for weekly/quarterly payroll peaks. Strong security posture: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency in US. Legal requires clear credit schedule for downtime and defined maintenance windows + 24/7 escalation path.
sla_negotiation_points: Uptime target: Aurora requesting 99.99% for production endpoints (we currently standard 99.95% for Dedicated)
Credit schedule: they want credits >= 10% of monthly fee for any monthly uptime <99.99%; tiered credits for 99.95-99.99/99.9-99.95/ <99.9
Maintenance windows: propose monthly 2-hour off-peak with 14-day notice; Aurora wants fewer windows and greater notice; emergency maintenance requires 48h notice and optional rollback
Support response times: P1 1 hour response and on-call engineer; P2 4 hours; P3 24 hours - Aurora insists these be in SLA
Planned vs unplanned: clarify that planned maint windows excluded from uptime calculation if 14-day notice given
Data residency and KMS: formal attestation + timeline for integration, included in SOW
technical_requirements: Reserved capacity: initial 12 A100-equivalent GPUs, autoscale to additional 12 as burst pool; documented ramp and billing for burst
Latency SLOs: p95 <150ms, p99 <350ms for chat workloads; embeddings throughput 250 reqs/sec target
Throughput: sustain 200k tokens/min baseline; burst 500k tokens/min for up to 30 minutes per event
Routing/fallback: must support routing to lower-cost model variant if primary capacity unavailable
KV/prefix caching: require compatibility with session cache across pods in VPC
Monitoring/tracing: per-request latency, token-level billing, and tracing hooks into Aurora observability stack
